newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares end little changed.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares end little changed.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swiss shares ended a quiet day little changed ahead of Roche's 1996 results and Tuesday's U.S. Fed meeting.
Prices were bolstered by firming futures on government bonds and a favourable German share market. But profit taking put shares under pressure towards the end of the session.
* Blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) added 6.0 points, or 0.13 percent, to 4,497.3 points.
* Broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) up 2.19 points, or 0.08 percent, to 2,856.83 points.
Roche said after the bourse closed that 1996 group net rose 16 percent to 3,899 million Swiss francs.
Traders said this was at the lower end of expectations. One trader called the result "slightly disappointing". Roche also proposed raising its dividend to 75 francs from 64 francs.
Most-traded Roche certificates lost 85 francs to 12,250. Dealers said Roche results are likely to influence the bourse in the next few sessions.
* Novartis registered shares ended up 11 francs to 1,714.
* Nestle, which will release its 1996 results on Wednesday, added four francs to 1,571. Analysts' median forecast is for net profit to rise around 10 percent to 3.23 billion.
* Among financials, attention focused on Credit Suisse Group CSHZn.S, which gave up some of its intra-day gains to end one franc up at 166.50 francs.
* ABB shares were up nine francs to 1,682 after it announced it was selling its refrigeration business to Denmark's Sabroe Regrigeration A/S for $93 million.
* Insurers Swiss Re, Winterthur and Zurich were slightly lower. Sulzer and Clariant were also among the day's losers.
* Stocks of inspection firm Surveillance continued their recent decline, slumping 70 francs, or 2.26 percent, to 3,030 francs.
* Trade was quiet on the Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchage (Soffex) as investors kept to the sidelines ahead of Easter and Tuesday's U.S. Fed meeting.

Volume was described as low. A total of 128,039 options changed hands, with UBS and Winterthur seeing most interest. The call/put ratio stood at one to 1.25. Implicit volatilites decreased slightly, dealers said.
On the futures side, 2,568 SMI contracts were traded, most of which were April SMI futures. The April SMI was up 9.5 points to 4,507.0 points.
